descriptionChirho: The proper noun Lachish (לָכִישׁ), referring to a major fortified Judean city in the Shephelah lowlands, prominent in both the conquest narratives (Joshua 10:3-35, 12:11) and the Assyrian/Babylonian siege accounts (2 Kings 18:14-17, 19:8; 2 Chr 11:9, 25:27, 32:9; Isa 36:2, 37:8; Jer 34:7; Mic 1:13; Neh 11:30). All 24 occurrences refer to the same geographic location in various prepositional frames: bare nominative (Lachish, 20x), with min 'from Lachish' (2x), and another min-prefixed usage rendered 'from Lachish' (2x). Multilingual evidence confirms a single referent: spa 'Laquis/de Laquis', hin 'लाकीश/लाकीश-को', arb 'لَخيشَ/مِن لَخيشَ', kor '라기스/라기시에서', swa 'Lakishi/kutoka Lakishi'. The grammatical variation reflects directional prepositions, not different senses.
